rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the singular al-watr as God; the author says related reports will follow.
rows.anchor: والوتر هو الله تعالى، وعلى هذه الأقوال روايات ستوافيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take paired and odd as even and odd numbers, recalling the blessing of measuring quantities by number.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد الزوج والفرد من العدد، وفي الإقسام بهما تذكير بالعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the pair and odd as all creatures, since things are either paired or singular.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشفع والوتر جميع المخلوقات لأن الأشياء إما زوج وإما فرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported interpretation calls Adam the odd one, paired with his wife.
rows.anchor: وقيل الوتر آدم شفع بزوجته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A view calls days and nights the pair and Resurrection Day the single day after which no night comes.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشفع الأيام والليالي والوتر اليوم الذي لا ليل بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations pair al-Safa with al-Marwa and call the Sacred House the odd one.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشفع الصفا والمروة والوتر البيت الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation pairs the days of ʿAd with their nights as the odd counterpart.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشفع أيام عاد والوتر لياليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view pairs Paradise's eight gates with Hell's seven gates.
rows.anchor: وقيل الشفع أبواب الجنة وهي ثمانية والوتر أبواب جهنم وهي سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes many further readings, counted by some as thirty-six, and judges most to be arbitrary.
rows.anchor: أنهاها بعضهم إلى ستة وثلاثين قولا ولا يخلو أكثرها من تحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasri means passes on, as in 74:33; the definite article is generic, so the oath concerns the end of night generally.
rows.anchor: { والليل إذا يسر } أي يمضي فهو كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported alternative identifies the night as the Night of Sacrifice, when pilgrims travel from Arafat to Muzdalifa and then Mina; the author finds this implausible, especially if the ten nights are the first ten nights.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد به ليلة المزدلفة وهي ليلة النحر التي يسري فيها الحاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question points back to the preceding oaths and seeks assent: they suffice for a rational person to distinguish truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: الإشارة بذلك إلى ما تقدم من القسم، والاستفهام للتقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God swears only by something honored, His oath confirms a truth whose veracity is beyond doubt.
rows.anchor: ولا يقسم إلا بما له شرف ومنزلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is omitted and signaled by the later punishment of the arrogant and reward of tranquil souls; this allusive omission intensifies warning and glad tidings.
rows.anchor: وجواب الأقسام المذكورة محذوف يدل عليه ما سيذكر من عذاب أهل الطغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's giving or withholding is a trial and examination, as the omitted oath-answer indicates.
rows.anchor: وأن إنعامه تعالى على من أنعم عليه وإمساكه عنه فيمن أمسك إنما هو ابتلاء وامتحان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ʿAd are the earlier people of Hud, repeatedly recounted in the Qur'an and associated with al-Ahqaf; their story was discussed under Hud.
rows.anchor: هم عاد الأولى قوم هود تكررت قصتهم في القرآن الكريم وأشير إلى أنهم كانوا بالأحقاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading makes Iram a prosperous, unmatched city of the people, with lofty palaces and extended columns; surviving reports cannot establish further details beyond the Qur'an's summary.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآيتين أن إرم كانت مدينة لهم معمورة عديمة النظير ذات قصور عالية وعمد ممددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify Iram with the ʿAd people, named for their forefather, and take “pillars” to mean their strength and might.
rows.anchor: قوم عاد - وهو في الأصل اسم أبيهم سموا باسم أبيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming of the Lord may mean the coming of His command, supported by 2:210 alongside 16:33; this requires an omitted “command” or a rational metaphor for attributing coming to God.
rows.anchor: وعليه فهناك مضاف محذوف والتقدير جاء أمر ربك أو نسبة المجيء إليه تعالى من المجاز العقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bringing Hell means making it appear to them, as in passages where it is exposed to those who see or go astray and the veil is removed.
rows.anchor: لا يبعد أن يكون المراد بالمجيء بجهنم إبرازها لهم كما في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection, people remember fully that worldly good and evil were God's test and that they fell short.
rows.anchor: أن ما كان يؤتاه في الحياة الدنيا من خير أو شر كان من ابتلاء الله وامتحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “how can remembrance help?” is a figure for its uselessness: on the day of recompense there is no return for repentance or good works.
rows.anchor: فإن الذكرى إنما تنفع فيما أمكنه أن يتدارك ما فرط فيه بتوبة وعمل صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “My life” means the afterlife, the real life, as 29:64 says; what one should have sent ahead is righteous work for it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتقديم للحياة تقديم العمل الصالح للحياة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish is made when the person remembers the Resurrection and sees that nothing can benefit him.
rows.anchor: وما في الآية تمن يتمناه الإنسان عندما يتذكر يوم القيامة ويشاهد أنه لا ينفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the ordinary reading, the pronouns refer to God: no creature can inflict or bind with punishment like His, a forceful threat.
rows.anchor: ضميرا عذابه ووثاقه لله تعالى والمعنى فيومئذ لا يعذب عذاب الله أحد من الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading with fatḥa on the dhāl and thāʾ makes the pronouns refer to the human: none is punished or bound as severely as that person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ { لا يعذب } بفتح الذال و { ولا يوثق } بفتح الثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tranquil soul rests in God, accepts His choices, knows itself to be God's servant, and sees worldly gain and loss as a test; it neither grows arrogant through blessings nor ungrateful in poverty.
rows.anchor: هي التي تسكن إلى ربها وترضى بما رضي به فترى نفسها عبدا لا يملك لنفسه شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such a soul remains in steady servitude, avoiding excess and neglect, unlike the worldly and rebellious person described earlier.
rows.anchor: بل هو في مستقر من العبودية لا ينحرف عن مستقيم صراطه بإفراط أو تفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to return spans from revival through settlement in Paradise, or from death to entry into the eternal garden, rather than occurring only after judgment as some say.
rows.anchor: وليس خطابا واقعا بعد الحساب كما ذكره بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is content because trust in God entails acceptance of His decrees and law; God is pleased when the servant stays within servanthood.
rows.anchor: وتوصيفها بالراضية لأن اطمئنانها إلى ربها يستلزم رضاها بما قدر وقضى تكوينا أو حكم به تشريعا

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: The “watchpost” is a bridge over the Path that no servant can cross while owing another person an injustice.
rows.anchor: وفيه عن الصادق عليه السلام أنه قال المرصاد قنطرة على الصراط لا يجوزها عبد بمظلمة عبد

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: In explaining Jonah's fear that God would not constrain him, the report says qadara means to be certain God would not constrict his provision; 89:16 uses it for narrowing provision.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام في حديث في تفسير قوله تعالى { وذا النون إذ ذهب مغاضبا فظن أن لن نقدر عليه } إنما ظن بمعنى استيقن

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar explains the earth being pounded repeatedly as an earthquake.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { كلا إذا دكت الأرض دكا دكا } قال هي الزلزلة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says Hell will be led on the Day of Resurrection by seventy thousand reins held by seventy thousand angels; it would burn the heavens and earth if God did not restrain it. The report is also transmitted from Abu Saʿid and Ibn Masʿud and through a Shia chain from ʿAli.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: الإمام الرضا
rows.claim: The Imam says God is not described as coming or going, since He is exalted above movement; “your Lord came” means His command came.
rows.anchor: عن علي بن فضال عن أبيه قال سألت الرضا عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A believer is not coerced at death: the Angel reassures him and shows him Muhammad, ʿAli, Fatima, al-Hasan, al-Husayn and the Imams; a caller invites the soul, content with their guardianship and reward, to return and enter their company and Paradise. The report also appears in al-Qummi and al-Barqi.
rows.anchor: عن سدير الصيرفي قال قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kabad means toil and hardship; human life is pervaded by effort, since worldly goods are never obtained in pure pleasure but mixed with distress, struggle, and calamity.
rows.anchor: الكبد الكد والتعب، والجملة جواب القسم فاشتمال الكبد على خلق الإنسان وإحاطة الكد والتعب به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thought that nobody can overpower him follows from human toil: people are frustrated in their wishes and dominated by the One who determines their affairs, so God can act upon them as He wills.
rows.anchor: والذي يغلبه في إرادته ويقهره على التلبس بما قدر له وهو الله سبحانه يقدر عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human frustration should prevent arrogance toward God and excuses for boasting about, withholding, or ostentatiously spending wealth.
rows.anchor: فليس للإنسان أن يحسب أن لن يقدر عليه أحد فيدعوه ذلك إلى أن يعلو على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The context suggests a person who professed or approached Islam had spent money and boasted of wasting a great deal; God answers that salvation requires the difficult charity and joining the believers.
rows.anchor: مشعر بأنه كان هناك بعض من أظهر الإسلام أو مال إليه فقد أنفق بعض ماله وامتن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Boasting of vast spending implies imagining God did not see it; God sees what was spent, but spending alone is insufficient without harder acts of servitude and solidarity with believers.
rows.anchor: أن لازم إخبار الإنسان بإهلاكه مالا لبدا أنه يحسب أنا في غفلة وجهل بما أنفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God equipped the person with eyes, a tongue, and lips: the eyes acquire knowledge of visible things, while speech communicates inner knowledge to others.
rows.anchor: جهزناه في بدنه بما يبصر به فيحصل له العلم بالمرئيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught the two paths by inspiration: people recognize good and distinguish it from evil, as in 91:7–8.
rows.anchor: علمناه طريق الخير وطريق الشر بإلهام منا فهو يعرف الخير ويميزه من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eyes, tongue, and moral inspiration show that God knows actions, intentions, and their moral quality; it is incoherent to think He fails to see or distinguish them.
rows.anchor: فهو تعالى يرى ما عمله الإنسان ويعلم ما ينويه بعمله ويميز كونه خيرا أو شرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqtiham is swift, forceful entry; the steep, difficult mountain path figures the hardship of spending, as the passage will explain.
rows.anchor: الاقتحام الدخول بسرعة وضغط وشدة، والعقبة الطريق الصعب الوعر الذي فيه صعود من الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence is not a curse wishing that the boastful person would fail to climb the obstacle.
rows.anchor: وقيل الجملة دعاء على الانسان القائل أهلكت مالا لبدا، وليس بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What will make you know the obstacle?” magnifies its importance, as in similar Qur'anic formulas.
rows.anchor: تفخيم لشأنها كما مر في نظائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a neck means emancipating a slave; alternatively the obstacle itself is emancipation, so climbing it is performing that very act. This rejects an interpretation requiring an omitted word for “climbing.”
rows.anchor: هي أي العقبة فك رقبة فالمراد بالعقبة نفس الفك الذي هو العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Freeing a neck and feeding during famine are instances of extending mercy, singled out for their importance; freeing slaves is named first because religion gives it special concern.
rows.anchor: من مصاديق نشر الرحمة خص بالذكر لمكان الأهمية، وقدم فك الرقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masghaba is famine, maq'raba is kinship, and matraba describes one pressed to the dirt through extreme poverty; the verse calls for feeding a related orphan or destitute person.
rows.anchor: المسغبة المجاعة، والمقربة القرابة بالنسب، والمتربة من التراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy is a verbal noun: believers urge one another to patience in obedience to God and compassion toward the poor, needy, and destitute.
rows.anchor: والتواصي بالمرحمة وصية بعضهم بعضا بالرحمة على ذوي الفقر والفاقة والمسكنة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: When people said the two paths meant the mother's breasts, ʿAli answered that they mean good and evil.
rows.anchor: قيل لأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام إن أناسا يقولون في قوله { وهديناه النجدين } أنهما الثديان

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Kafi reports the Imam explaining the two heights as the paths of good and evil; similar reports are transmitted from ʿAli, Anas, Abu Umama, and others from the Prophet, and in al-Qummi.
rows.anchor: عن حمزة بن محمد عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله تعالى { وهديناه النجدين } قال نجد الخير والشر

rows.speaker: الإمام الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Ridha would save the best food for the poor, recite the obstacle verse, and explain that God provided a path to Paradise for people unable to free a slave: feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: عن جعفر بن خلاد قال كان أبو الحسن الرضا عليه السلام إذا أكل أتي بصحفة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In a report from al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib, the Prophet distinguishes freeing a whole slave oneself from helping pay for another's emancipation; he also recommends aid to unjust kin, feeding the hungry, giving drink, enjoining good, forbidding wrong, or at minimum speaking only good.
rows.anchor: وروي مرفوعا عن البراء بن عازب قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Al-Qummi explains the dust-covered poor person as someone with nothing to shield him from the dirt.
rows.anchor: قال لا يقيه من التراب شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah teaches that flourishing comes through purifying the soul with piety, while failure comes from corrupting it; Thamud's destruction for denying Salih and hamstringing the she-camel warns Mecca. Its context indicates a Meccan surah.
rows.anchor: تذكر السورة أن فلاح الانسان - وهو يعرف التقوى والفجور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Duha is the sun's spreading and the day's extension, and the time takes its name from that; the oath is by the sun and its light spread over earth.
rows.anchor: الضحى انبساط الشمس وامتداد النهار وسمي الوقت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The moon follows the sun either by deriving its light from it, a constant state, or by rising after sunset, from crescent to fullness.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتلوه لها إن كان كسبه النور منها فالحال حال دائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to earth: daytime reveals it to sight. The alternative takes day as agent and the sun as object, but this reverses the fact that the sun causes daylight.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضمير الفاعل في { جلاها } للنهار وضمير المفعول للشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposals refer the pronoun to the world or darkness, or make God the agent and sun the object; the author calls these distant readings.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير المؤنث للدنيا، وقيل للظلمة، وقيل ضمير الفاعل لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night covers earth, as in the preceding verse; taking the object as the sun is implausible because night covers earth and what is upon it.
rows.anchor: أي يغطي الأرض، فالضمير للأرض كما في { جلاها } وقيل للشمس وهو بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense for night, unlike the past tense for day, evokes the current veiling of the earth by sin at the early Islamic mission and also preserves the rhyme.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على الحال ليكون فيه إيماء إلى غشيان الفجور الأرض في الزمن الحاضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “what” in “what built it” and “what spread it” is relative; God is the wondrous builder and spreader, with “what” chosen to suggest majesty. Reading it as a verbal noun is weak because the context continues with “the soul and what formed it.”
rows.anchor: و { ما } في { وما بناها } و { ما طحاها } موصولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul and its shaper are sworn by: the shaper has power, knowledge, and wisdom to order its creation and balance its faculties.
rows.anchor: واقسم بنفس والشيء ذي القدرة والعلم والحكمة الذي سواها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the indefinite “soul” as indefinite; others see it as honorific, and the author allows that it may signal that the soul has a distinctive description and significance.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { نفس } قيل للتنكير، وقيل للتفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “does not fear its consequence” most likely does not refer to the wretched camel-killer or to Salih; both alternatives are visibly weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل ضمير { لا يخاف } للأشقى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi glosses the shaping of the soul as its creation and formation.
rows.anchor: بحث روائي في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Zurarah, Humran, and Muhammad ibn Muslim report from al-Baqir and al-Sadiq that God showed the soul what it should do and leave.
rows.anchor: روى زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The same report glosses success as obedience and failure as disobedience.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى { قد أفلح من زكاها } قال قد أفلح من أطاع

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A man asks whether people's present effort was predestined or whether their future obedience to the Prophet was a test; the Prophet answers that it was decreed, and those destined for either end are prepared for its work.
rows.anchor: أخرج أحمد ومسلم وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن مردويه عن عمران بن حصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's response means prior decree necessitates an act from the perspective of divine determination without removing its possibility and choice from the human perspective; the book has explained this before.
rows.anchor: لا ينافي إمكان صدوره بالنظر إلى الإنسان واختياره

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says a soul succeeds if God purifies it and fails if God deprives it of every good.
rows.anchor: أفلحت نفس زكاها الله وخابت نفس خيبها الله من كل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing purification and deprivation to God does not negate their attribution to human obedience and disobedience; divine misguidance is retributive, as 2:26 says.
rows.anchor: وإنما ينتسب إلى الله سبحانه من الإضلال ما كان على طريق المجازاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: In a report judged sound by al-Majmaʿ, the Prophet says the earliest people’s most wretched was the camel-killer and the later people’s was the one who would strike ʿAli's head; variants name ʿAmmar and phrase it as ʿAli's killer.
rows.anchor: عن عثمان بن صهيب عن أبيه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah warns by contrasting divergent efforts: generous, pious believers who affirm the good promise reach lasting happiness, while misers who claim self-sufficiency deny it and approach misery; financial giving receives special emphasis. The surah may be Meccan or Medinan.
rows.anchor: غرض السورة الإنذار وتسلك إليه بالإشارة إلى اختلاف مساعي الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night swallows the day, as in 13:3; it may instead be understood as covering earth or sun.
rows.anchor: إقسام بالليل إذا يغشى النهار على حد قوله تعالى يغشي الليل النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is said to have become manifest in the past tense while the night “covers” in the present, following the explanation given for the opening of the preceding surah.
rows.anchor: والتعبير عن صفة الليل بالمضارع وعن صفة النهار بالماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “what” that created male and female is God, expressed with an honorific ambiguity; the sexes are universal, rather than only human beings or Adam and Eve. Taking “what” as a verbal noun is weak.
rows.anchor: و { ما } موصولة والمراد به الله سبحانه وإنما عبر بما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿy is swift walking and here means purposeful deeds; shatta is a plural meaning dispersed. The oath answers that efforts and their effects diverge, from generosity, piety, and faith to miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial.
rows.anchor: السعي هو المشي السريع، والمراد به العمل من حيث يهتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving means spending for God; piety specifies religious giving. “The best” is the promised reward for such spending and entails faith in resurrection, God's unity, and the message that conveys His promise.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن التقدير بالعدة الحسنى وهي ما وعد الله من الثواب على الانفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together the two verses describe belief in God, His Messenger, and the Last Day, with spending for God to seek the reward promised by the Messenger.
rows.anchor: ومحصل الآيتين أن يكون مؤمنا بالله ورسوله واليوم الآخر وينفق المال لوجه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the person ready for the ease-filled afterlife and Paradise through righteous deeds fits the Qur'an's promises better than merely making good works easier to perform.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني أقرب وأوضح انطباقا على ما هو المعهود من مواعد القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Miserliness opposes giving; self-sufficiency is seeking wealth by hoarding, and denying the good promise means rejecting the reward preached by the messengers, hence denying resurrection.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالتكذيب بالحسنى الكفر بالعدة الحسنى وثواب الله الذي بلغه الأنبياء والرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made ready for difficulty means being denied success in good works through their burden and an unwelcoming heart toward faith, or being prepared for punishment.
rows.anchor: بتيسيره للعسرى خذلانه بعدم توفيقه للأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarradda is falling from a height and by extension destruction; the fall may be into the grave, Hell, or simply death. The question asks what his wealth could do, or states that it will do nothing.
rows.anchor: التردي هو السقوط من مكان عال ويطلق على الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of both the last and first life explains the prior facilitation or concisely announces it: He guides because guidance is His responsibility and no obstacle can prevent Him.
rows.anchor: تعليل لما تقدم من حديث تيسيره لليسرى وللعسرى أو الإخبار به بأوجز بيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created people to worship Him and made worship a straight path to Him, commanding it through His messengers.
rows.anchor: أنه خلقهم ليعبدوه كما قال وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has undertaken to show people His way—whether they follow it or leave it—through verses on the clear and crooked paths, truth, and the choice to be grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: قضى على نفسه أن يبين لهم سبيله ويهديهم إليه بمعنى إراءة الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic guidance is also permitted guidance toward the path, as in 42:52 and 12:108; the author refers to an earlier rational discussion of prophethood.
rows.anchor: هذا في الهداية بمعنى إراءة الطريق وأما الهداية بمعنى الإيصال إلى المطلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance as showing the road is God's responsibility, while guidance as bringing people to their desired end is God's creative act; its outcomes include good life now and eternal happiness, promised in 20:123, 16:97, and 4:122.
rows.anchor: فمن البين أنه من قبيل الصنع والإيجاد الذي يختص به تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's original guidance can also be attributed secondarily to other causes by permission; this does not conflict with its attribution to Him.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي انتساب هذا المعنى من الهداية إليه تعالى بنحو الأصالة انتسابه إلى غيره تعالى بنحو التبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the evil person ready for difficulty is required to distinguish impure from pure and gather the impure into Hell.
rows.anchor: وأما التيسير للعسرى فهو مما يتوقف عليه التيسير لليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an guides all but is healing and mercy for believers, while it only increases wrongdoers' loss.
rows.anchor: ولا يزيد الظالمين إلا خسارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Only the most wretched enters it” denies lasting residence in the Fire to anyone but unbelievers; it does not deny that sinful believers may enter temporarily.
rows.anchor: الآية إنما تنفي عن غير الكافر الخلود فيها دون أصل الدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “most pious” means the person more God-fearing than others, including those wary of worldly loss or poverty: among them, the one who spends for God is most pious. The descriptor makes the interpretation general, without excluding a specific occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأتقى من هو أتقى من غيره ممن يتقي المخاطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making “most pious” and “most wretched” absolute superlatives over all people implies that only one person, or one per age, is saved or damned, which conflicts with the general warning to everyone.
rows.anchor: فلا معنى لأن يقال أنذرتكم جميعا نارا لا يخلد فيها إلا واحد منكم جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pious person gives and spends wealth to make himself grow in purity.
rows.anchor: الذي يعطي وينفق ماله يطلب بذلك أن ينمو نماء صالحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one has a favor owed in repayment for the gift; he gives only for God, as the next verse confirms.
rows.anchor: ليس لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى تلك النعمة بما يؤتيه من المال

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: A report glosses male and female as the two spouses, “gave” as the palm tree, and belief in the best promise as what is with the Messenger; al-Qummi also relates it anonymously.
rows.anchor: وقوله الزوجين تفسير منه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qummi identifies the person “most pious” as Abu al-Dahdah, an interpretation the author says comes through Shia routes from the Imams.
rows.anchor: في قوله تعالى { وسيجنبها الأتقى } قال أبو الدحداح

rows.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi transmits from al-Wahidi a story in which an Ansari buys a palm tree for forty trees and gives it to the Prophet, who gives it to the home's owner.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس وفيه أن الانصاري ساوم صاحب النخلة في نخلته

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: A report from ʿAta names the man Abu al-Dahdah; al-Suyuti transmits the story from Ibn ʿAbbas through Ibn Abi Hatim and calls it weak.
rows.anchor: ثم روى الطبرسي عن عطاء أن اسم الرجل أبو الدحداح، وروى السيوطي

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says Sunni exegetes agree the “most pious” is Abu Bakr; he says Shia exegetes instead name ʿAli, citing 5:55, and interpret the superlative as the best human.
rows.anchor: أجمع المفسرون منا على أن المراد منه - يعني من الأتقى - أبو بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects as an overstatement the claim that all Shia sources name ʿAli; he says the reliable Shia evidence supports Abu al-Dahdah and again rejects an absolute “best of all people” reading.
rows.anchor: أما ما نسب إلى الشيعة بأسرهم من القول فالمعتمد عليه من طرقهم صحيح الحميري المتقدم

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A weak report through al-Barqi applies “most pious” to the Prophet and his follower, the giving description to ʿAli, and the next verse to the Prophet; the author calls this application rather than exegesis because it disrupts the syntax. If “who gives” belongs to the verse, the report would imply rejected textual alteration.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ومن تبعه

rows.speaker: الإمام الرضا
rows.claim: The Imam says God guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills, rejecting companions' claim that knowledge is acquired by reasoning; the report appeals to Banu Hashim's closeness and right to the matter.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال، قلت قول الله تبارك وتعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance as bringing a person to the end belongs to God as Lord; misguidance also belongs to Him only as retributive withholding of mercy, not as initial misguidance.
rows.anchor: وأما الإضلال والمراد به الإضلال على سبيل المجازاة دون الإضلال الابتدائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah was said to follow several days without revelation, when people said the Prophet's Lord had forsaken him; it came to console him. The surah could be Meccan or Medinan.
rows.anchor: قيل انقطع الوحي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أياما حتى قالوا إن ربه ودعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath is by duha, the sun's spread and the day's extension, and by the night at rest as its darkness covers the world.
rows.anchor: والضحى - على ما في المفردات - انبساط الشمس وامتداد النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waddaʿa means to bid farewell, and qalā means to hate or hate intensely; the oath's answer fits the contrast between daytime light and nighttime darkness with the arrival and pause of revelation.
rows.anchor: التوديع الترك، والقلى بكسر القاف البغض أو شدته، والآية جواب القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife being better is an ascent from the preceding reassurance: the Prophet remains in divine favor throughout earthly life, and his next life is better than this one.
rows.anchor: في معنى الترقي بالنسبة إلى ما تفيده الآية السابقة من كونه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على ما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of a gift that will satisfy him reaffirms that the afterlife is better; it promises an unrestricted gift followed by unrestricted satisfaction.
rows.anchor: تقرير وتثبيت لقوله { وللآخرة خير لك من الأولى } وقد اشتمل الوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the promise looks to both lives rather than only the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقيل الآية ناظرة إلى الحياتين جميعا دون الحياة الآخرة فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favors include caring for the Prophet after his father died before birth, his mother died when he was two, and his grandfather guardian died when he was eight, after which his uncle raised him.
rows.anchor: فقد مات أبوه وهو في بطن أمه ثم ماتت أمه وهو ابن سنتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation understands “orphan” figuratively as a unique pearl without peer, whom people gathered around.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد باليتيم الوحيد الذي لا نظير له في الناس كما يقال در يتيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's “being astray” means lacking guidance in himself considered apart from God's gift; like all creation he had no guidance except through God, even though divine guidance accompanied him from his beginning.
rows.anchor: فلا هدى له صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولا لأحد من الخلق إلا بالله سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A quoted statement says God chose the Hereafter over the world for the Prophet's household and connects that choice to the promise that the Prophet will be satisfied.
rows.anchor: إنا أهل بيت اختار الله لنا الآخرة على الدنيا

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet saw Fatima grinding grain in a rough camel-hair garment and urged her to endure worldly bitterness for the next life's blessing; God then revealed 93:5. The author allows that this verse descended later as an insertion or was revealed again alone.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال دخل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم على فاطمة وهي تطحن بالرحى

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Through Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, ʿAli reports the Prophet affirming that the intercession discussed by the Iraqis is true; the excerpt breaks before the rest of the report.
rows.anchor: حدثني عمي محمد بن الحنفية عن علي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah directs the Prophet to work hard for God and desire Him, after reminding him of divine beneficence.
rows.anchor: أمر بالنصب في الله والرغبة اليه توصل إليه بتقدمة الامتنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah could be Meccan or Medinan, but its context fits the Medinan period better.
rows.anchor: والسورة تحتمل المكية والمدنية وسياق آياتها أوفق للمدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Imams, Tawus, and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz say al-Duha and al-Sharh are one surah; al-Razi rejects this because he thinks the first concerns distress while “expanding the chest” implies a cheerful state.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات عن أئمة أهل البيت عليهم السلام أن الضحى وألم نشرح سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Razi's equation of an expanded chest with happiness: it means capacity to receive truths, revelations, and harm in preaching, so the passages can coexist.
rows.anchor: المراد بشرح صدره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في الآية جعله بحيث يسع ما يلقى إليه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the Prophet asked why earlier prophets were granted special powers; God answered by reminding him that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him, expanded his chest, and lifted his burden.
rows.anchor: ما رواه ابن أبي حاتم عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sharh literally means opening or spreading flesh; for the chest it means an opening through divine light, tranquility, and spirit, as in 20:25, 94:1, and 39:22.
rows.anchor: أصل الشرح بسط اللحم ونحوه يقال شرحت اللحم وشرحته ومنه شرح الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence of three blessings, the hardship-ease explanation repeated, and the closing commands shows that expanded chest means capacity for revelation, preaching, and the resulting persecution.
rows.anchor: كل ذلك يشهد على كون المراد بشرح صدره صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بسطه بحيث يسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A burden is a heavy load; “making the back creak” evokes pressure so great it produces an audible sound, hence the burden's palpable weight.
rows.anchor: الوزر الحمل الثقيل، وإنقاض الظهر كسره بحيث يسمع له صوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lifting the burden removes its felt weight; the phrase is coordinated with “did We not expand your chest,” which implicitly means “We have expanded it.”
rows.anchor: ووضع الوزر إذهاب ما يحس من ثقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, lifting the Prophet's burden means making his mission succeed by arranging the means for his struggle; the message and its call are the load he carried after his chest was expanded.
rows.anchor: إنفاذ دعوته وإمضاء مجاهدته في الله بتوفيق الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported explanations include the chest-splitting tradition, pre-prophetic acts, lack of knowledge of revealed law, uncertainty about fulfilling the mission, and the early weight of revelation.
rows.anchor: وقيل وضع الوزر إشارة إلى ما وردت به الرواية أن ملكين نزلا عليه وفلقا صدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed burdens are distress at people's misguidance, their persecution, grief over Abu Talib and Khadija, sin removed by infallibility, or the community's sin forgiven for him; the author calls some foolish, others weak and out of context.
rows.anchor: وهذه الوجوه بعضها سخيف وبعضها ضعيف لا يلائم السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the Prophet's mention above others, pairing his name with God's in the two testimonies and requiring every Muslim to mention him in each of the five daily prayers; the lift follows the burden poetically.
rows.anchor: ومن رفع ذكره أن قرن الله اسمه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم باسمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ease explains how God lifted the mission's burden and raised a name that rejectors tried to erase: He helped people accept the call, following His practice of changing events and conditions.
rows.anchor: فوضع الله وزره الذي حمله بتوفيق الناس لإجابة دعوته ورفع ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article on hardship is generic rather than exhaustive, and ease follows hardship in sequence rather than coexisting in time; the underlying rule is the changing, impermanent nature of events.
rows.anchor: فاللام في { العسر } للجنس دون الاستغراق ولعل السنة سنة تحول الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the initial fa explanatory and reads the passage as consolation through a gracious promise.
rows.anchor: وعن الزمخشري في الكشاف أن الفاء في { فإن مع العسر } الخ فصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explanation says pagans mocked the believers' poverty, making the Prophet fear people rejected Islam for that reason, and reads ease as later spoils. The author rejects this: the Prophet knew rejection came from arrogance, and people stayed opposed after Muslim power and wealth grew.
rows.anchor: وظاهره أن اللام في العسر للعهد دون الجنس وأن المراد باليسر ما رزقه الله المؤمنين بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the surah is taken as Meccan, ease may plausibly mean Islam's later strength and elevation after weakness.
rows.anchor: ولو حمل اليسر بعد العسر على شوكة الإسلام ورفعته بعد ضعته مع أخذ السورة مكية لم يكن به كثير بأس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the sentence confirms and strengthens it; treating it as a new sentence is another view. The claim that one definite hardship yields two separate eases relies on a grammatical rule that is not universal.
rows.anchor: تكرار للتأكيد والتثبيت وقيل استئناف وذكروا أن في الآيتين دلالة على أن مع العسر الواحد يسران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tanwin on ease marks a kind or type, not magnitude, and “with” means subsequent sequence rather than simultaneous timing.
rows.anchor: والتنوين في { يسرا } للتنويع لا للتفخيم كما ذكره بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the mission assigned by God, the Prophet should exert himself in worship and supplication and desire God's reward; the commands follow from the earlier loading, favor, and subsequent ease.
rows.anchor: إذا كان العسر يأتي بعده اليسر والأمر فيه إلى الله لا غير فإذا فرغت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Specific applications include finishing obligatory prayers and performing supererogatory worship, finishing prayer and supplicating, completing military service and worshipping, or leaving worldly tasks for the afterlife; the author treats the first two as instances and the rest as weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد إذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في النوافل، وقيل إذا فرغت من الصلاة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: When Abu Hurayra asks about the first sign of prophethood, the Prophet recounts two figures splitting his chest in the wilderness, removing envy and inserting mercy. Versions say he was ten or twenty years old, or place the event at the first revelation or the Night Journey; the author treats it as a symbolic vision, rejecting strained material explanations.
rows.anchor: أخرج عبد الله بن أحمد في زوائد الزهد عن ابي بن كعب أن أبا هريرة قال يا رسول الله ما أول ما رأيت

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Jibril tells the Prophet that God raised his mention by ensuring that whenever God is mentioned, the Prophet is mentioned with Him.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو يعلى وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن حبان وابن مردويه وأبو نعيم في الدلائل عن أبي سعيد الخدري

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reports that the Prophet came out happy and laughing, saying that one hardship will not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: والحاكم والبيهقي عن الحسن قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: The Imams explain the command as finishing the prescribed prayer, devoting oneself to supplication to the Lord, and earnestly asking Him for one's need.
rows.anchor: وهو المروي عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah argues for resurrection and recompense from humanity's best form and later descent: some remain on original nature while others fall low, and wisdom requires distinguishing them in reward. It is Meccan or possibly Medinan; “this secure city” supports Mecca but is not conclusive.
rows.anchor: تذكر السورة البعث والجزاء وتسلك إليه من طريق خلق الإنسان في أحسن تقويم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Views on the fig and olive include the familiar fruits with their many benefits, the two trees, or the mountains near Damascus and Jerusalem; the mountains may take their names from those crops and be oaths for the regions where many prophets appeared. Other views also exist.
rows.anchor: قيل المراد بالتين والزيتون الفاكهتان المعروفتان أقسم الله بهما لما فيهما من الفوائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sinai is the mountain where God spoke with Moses, also called Sinai.
rows.anchor: والمراد بطور سينين الجبل الذي كلم الله تعالى فيه موسى بن عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secure city is Mecca because security is specially prescribed for the sanctuary; Abraham prays for it in 2:126 and 14:35. “Secure” can mean possessing safety or making people safe, with the latter attributing safety to the city figuratively.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهذا البلد الأمين مكة المشرفة لأن الأمن خاصة مشرعة للحرم وهي فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer says the human species has the best constitution in every respect; this means humanity is naturally fit to ascend to lasting bliss through useful knowledge and righteous deeds.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكون خلقه في أحسن تقويم اشتمال التقويم عليه في جميع شؤونه وجهات وجوده
